related_questions.question: How long do you have immunity after having COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: Immunity from a COVID-19 infection generally wanes after 3-4 months. While natural immunity from infection can offer some protection, research suggests that it has significantly decreased since the Omicron variant became dominant. It's also important to note that vaccines, while not fully preventing infection or mild symptoms, are effective at preventing severe disease.

Several factors influence the duration of immunity, including the specific variant of the virus, individual immune responses, and whether or not the individual was vaccinated. The Omicron variant, in particular, has shown a reduced ability to provide long-lasting immunity compared to earlier strains.

Therefore, even if someone has recently recovered from a COVID-19 infection, it's recommended to get vaccinated 3-4 months after recovery, especially if they haven't had the latest vaccine. The vaccines available offer better protection against severe illness than natural immunity alone.
